```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# HTML figures are drawn as PNG and kept as WebP: lossless (the same pixels in about half the space of PNG), or
# lossy at quality 90 when that is less than half the size, as for traces and densities of thousands of draws. The
# PDF figures stay vector graphics. Any failure of magick (not installed, no WebP, or a broken installation whose
# system libraries are missing) keeps the PNG
webp <- function(path) {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output() || !grepl(pattern = "[.]png$", x = path)) return(path)
  tryCatch(
      {
        if (!requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE) || !isTRUE(magick::magick_config()$webp)) return(path)
        img <- magick::image_read(path)
        out <- sub(pattern = "[.]png$", replacement = ".webp", x = path)
        tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".webp")
        magick::image_write(
            image   = img
          , path    = out
          , format  = "webp"
          , quality = 100
          , defines = c(`webp:lossless` = "true")
          )
        magick::image_write(image = img, path = tmp, format = "webp", quality = 90)
        if (file.size(tmp) < file.size(out) / 2) file.copy(from = tmp, to = out, overwrite = TRUE)
        unlink(c(path, tmp))
        out
      }
    , error = function(e) path
    )
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6,
                      dev = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "cairo_pdf" else "ragg_png", dpi = 96,
                      fig.process = webp)
if (requireNamespace("bayesammi", quietly = TRUE)) library(bayesammi) else
  pkgload::load_all(export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
```

# Abstract

Dozens of stability indices are in use, each computed once from the cell means of a trial. Computed on every
posterior draw of the cell means instead, each index gets a posterior mean, an HPD interval and, for every genotype,
a probability of being the best. `bam_indices()` does this for five classical indices and `bam_ammi_indices()` for
six AMMI-based ones. The cell means come from any fit: AMMI or GGE (`bayes_ammi()`) or a stability model
(`bayes_stability()`).

```{r fit}
fit <-
  bayes_ammi(
      .data   = Maiz
    , .y      = y
    , .gen    = entry
    , .env    = site
    , .rep    = rep
    , .nIter  = 3000
    , .k      = 2
    , .burnin = 500
    , .thin   = 1
    , .chains = 2
    , .priors = bam_priors(
          mu_mean     = 0
        , mu_var      = 1e+8
        , tau_mean    = 0
        , tau_var     = 1e+8
        , delta_mean  = 0
        , delta_var   = 1e+8
        , lambda_mean = 0
        , lambda_var  = 1e+8
        , nu          = 1
        , s2          = NULL
        )
    , .level  = 0.95
    , .seed   = 11
    , .align  = TRUE
    , .model  = "AMMI"
    , .het    = FALSE
    , .waic   = TRUE
    )
```

# Classical indices

For one draw of the cell means $\eta_{ij}$, with interaction
$\epsilon_{ij} = \eta_{ij} - \bar{\eta}_{i\cdot} - \bar{\eta}_{\cdot j} + \bar{\eta}_{\cdot\cdot}$:

| Index | Formula | Better |
|---|---|---|
| Wricke's ecovalence | $W_i = \sum_j \epsilon_{ij}^2$ | smaller |
| Shukla's stability variance | $\frac{G}{(G-2)(E-1)}W_i - \frac{\sum_k W_k}{(G-1)(G-2)(E-1)}$ | smaller |
| Lin and Binns' superiority | $\sum_j (\eta_{ij} - M_j)^2 / (2E)$, $M_j$ the best in environment $j$ | smaller |
| Annicchiarico's reliability | $\bar{Z}_i - z_{1-p} s_{Z_i}$, $Z_{ij} = 100\,\eta_{ij}/\bar{\eta}_{\cdot j}$ | larger |
| Eskridge's safety-first | $\bar{\eta}_{i\cdot} - z_{1-\alpha} s_i$, $s_i^2$ the variance across environments | larger |

```{r ind}
ind <-
  bam_indices(
      fit           = fit
    , higher_better = TRUE
    , .prob         = 0.25
    , .alpha        = 0.05
    )
ind
```

```{r ind-plot, fig.height = 6}
plot(x = ind)
```

```{r agree, include = FALSE}
m <- ind$means
rc <- round(x = cor(x = m$wricke, y = m$lin_binns, method = "spearman"), digits = 2)
neg <- ind$indices[index == "shukla" & lower < 0, .N]
```

The indices measure different things. Wricke's and Shukla's indices measure stability alone and rank genotypes in
the same order. Lin and Binns' index measures distance from the best, so it mixes mean and stability. The rank
correlation between Wricke's and Lin and Binns' posterior means is `r rc`. Shukla's estimator can be negative, as in
the classical analysis; `r neg` of its 9 HPD intervals reach below zero, a sign that the stability variance of those
genotypes cannot be told from zero.

Because the indices are computed from the cell means, without plot error, they describe the stability of the
expected performance. The HPD intervals show how well 20 environments determine them; they are wide.

# AMMI-based indices

With coordinates $\mathrm{PC}_{ik} = \lambda_k^{1/2}\alpha_{ik}$ and the share
$\theta_k = \lambda_k^2/\sum_m \lambda_m^2$ of each fitted term:

| Index | Formula | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ASV | $\sqrt{(\lambda_1^2/\lambda_2^2\,\mathrm{PC}_{i1})^2 + \mathrm{PC}_{i2}^2}$ | Purchase et al. (2000) |
| SIPC | $\sum_k \lvert\mathrm{PC}_{ik}\rvert$ | Sneller et al. (1997) |
| EV | $\sum_k \alpha_{ik}^2 / K$ | Zobel (1994) |
| Za | $\sum_k \theta_k \lvert\alpha_{ik}\rvert$ | Zali et al. (2012) |
| WAAS | $\sum_k \theta_k \lvert\mathrm{PC}_{ik}\rvert$ | Olivoto et al. (2019) |
| WAASY | mean and WAAS rescaled to 0-100 and weighted | Olivoto et al. (2019) |

```{r ai}
ai <-
  bam_ammi_indices(
      fit           = fit
    , higher_better = TRUE
    , .weight_y     = 50
    )
ai
```

```{r ai-plot, fig.height = 6}
plot(x = ai)
```

WAASY gives the mean and the stability equal weights (`.weight_y = 50`). A breeder who values the mean more raises the
weight:

```{r waasy}
data.table::rbindlist(
    l = lapply(
        X   = c(30, 50, 70)
      , FUN = function(wy) {
          a <-
            bam_ammi_indices(
                fit           = fit
              , higher_better = TRUE
              , .weight_y     = wy
              )
          a$indices[index == "WAASY"][order(-mean)][1:3, list(weight = wy, Gen, mean, prob_best)]
        }
      )
  )
```

# Indices from a stability model

The same classical indices can be computed from the cell means of a `bayes_stability()` fit:

```{r from-stab}
fs <-
  bayes_stability(
      .data   = Maiz
    , .y      = y
    , .gen    = entry
    , .env    = site
    , .rep    = rep
    , .model  = "ER"
    , .nIter  = 2000
    , .burnin = 500
    , .thin   = 1
    , .chains = 1
    , .priors = bam_stab_priors(
          mu_var = NULL
        , g_var  = NULL
        , h_var  = NULL
        , b_var  = 100
        , nu     = 1
        , s2     = NULL
        , nu_d   = 1
        , s2_d   = NULL
        )
    , .level  = 0.95
    , .alpha  = 0.05
    , .seed   = 11
    , .waic   = TRUE
    )
bam_indices(
    fit           = fs
  , higher_better = TRUE
  , .prob         = 0.25
  , .alpha        = 0.05
  )$means
```

# Interpretation

```{r int}
bam_interpret(
    x             = ind
  , higher_better = TRUE
  , top           = 5
  )
```

Shukla, G. K. (1972). Some statistical aspects of partitioning genotype-environmental components of variability. *Heredity*, 29(2), 237--245.

Lin, C. S. and Binns, M. R. (1988). A superiority measure of cultivar performance for cultivar x location data. *Canadian Journal of Plant Science*, 68(1), 193--198. doi:10.4141/cjps88-018

Annicchiarico, P. (1992). Cultivar adaptation and recommendation from alfalfa trials in Northern Italy. *Journal of Genetics and Breeding*, 46, 269--278.

Eskridge, K. M. (1990). Selection of stable cultivars using a safety-first rule. *Crop Science*, 30, 369--374.

Purchase, J. L., Hatting, H. and van Deventer, C. S. (2000). Genotype x environment interaction of winter wheat in South Africa: II. Stability analysis of yield performance. *South African Journal of Plant and Soil*, 17(3), 101--107.

Sneller, C. H., Kilgore-Norquest, L. and Dombek, D. (1997). Repeatability of yield stability statistics in soybean. *Crop Science*, 37(2), 383--390.

Zobel, R. W. (1994). Stress resistance and root systems. In *Proceedings of the Workshop on Adaptation of Plants to Soil Stress*, INTSORMIL Publication 94-2, 80--99. University of Nebraska-Lincoln.

Zali, H., Farshadfar, E., Sabaghpour, S. H. and Karimizadeh, R. (2012). Evaluation of genotype x environment interaction in chickpea using measures of stability from AMMI model. *Annals of Biological Research*, 3(7), 3126--3136.

Olivoto, T., Lucio, A. D. C., da Silva, J. A. G., Marchioro, V. S., de Souza, V. Q. and Jost, E. (2019). Mean performance and stability in multi-environment trials I: combining features of AMMI and BLUP techniques. *Agronomy Journal*, 111(6), 2949--2960. doi:10.2134/agronj2019.03.0220

Farshadfar, E. (2008). Incorporation of AMMI stability value and grain yield in a single non-parametric index (GSI) in bread wheat. *Pakistan Journal of Biological Sciences*, 11(14), 1791--1796.
